text: Create a ready-to-render context menu. The first argument to this hook describes the menu: The second, optional argument allows further customization of things like menu alignment. (See the examples section for more information.)
title: useContextMenu

text: The second parameter to useContextMenu can be used to control the context menu's alignment. Menu alignment can either be fixed (e.g. above/below/left/right) or relative to the cursor or target. Select an alignment: selected: above Click to demo: alignTo="above"
title: Alignment options

text: The recommended way to customize styles is to use CSS variables. Begin by customizing any of the variables below: Then just be sure to import the library styles once somewhere in your application. Default values are provided for any variables that are not defined. Global class names You can also bypass the included use-context-menu/styles.css file and define your own styles. Data selectors Lastly, data attribute selectors can be used to customize styles (although these are primarily intended for e2e testing purposes).
title: Custom styles

text: Menus can also be attached to the left-click action: Left-click the dropdown to open the menu: click to open Menus are also defined using the useContextMenu hook, but with an additional alignTo option: And they are attached to an element using the onClick prop instead of onContextMenu: Remember to import menu styles. See the custom styles page for more information.
title: Left-click menu

text: A context menu is shown by right-clicking an element: Right-click in the green box to open the context menu. Context menus are defined using the useContextMenu hook: And they can be attached to any element using the onContextMenu and onKeyDown props: Remember to import menu styles. See the custom styles page for more information.
title: Right-click menu

text: GitHub is the easiest place to look for help, but it's probably not the fastest. This project is maintained by a single developer so there is limited bandwidth for answering questions. I recommend asking questions on Stack Overflow or Reddit to start with. Both sites have active communities who often respond quickly. If you don't find an answer there you can try opening a GitHub issue- but please take a moment first to see if your question has has already been answered before opening a new one.
